newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea allows more fund issues for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea allows more fund issues for foreigners.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry said on Thursday domestic investment trust firms were allowed to issue beneficiary certificates for foreign investment in local stocks without limit until the end of June.
But a ministry statement said it plans to set limits on such issuances for the third quarter of this year and beyond.
The investment firms are also allowed to expand issuances of such certificates for foreign investment in local bonds up to a total of $973 million, against $400 million allowed in 1996.
Three Seoul-based firms of the nation's eight investment firms are now able to issue up to $150 million worth of certificates per company, up from $100 million in 1996.
The ceiling for each of the remaining five firms was raised to $50 million from $20 million in 1996, the statement said.
